humanities_role_explanation: Items are Seshat Databank records on historical societies, coded by history and archaeology experts and research assistants. They test graduate and expert-level historical knowledge directly, so the competence measured is disciplinary.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only. Each Seshat record is converted into a textual four-option multiple-choice question about a variable, a polity and a time frame.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Models answer whether a characteristic (e.g. writing, mutilation, professional military officers) was present, absent, inferred present or inferred absent for a polity and time frame. This is expert-level factual recall of history. The evidenced-versus-inferred distinction is part of the answer key. It is delivered as a 4-option multiple-choice question, with a 2-choice variant that keeps only present and absent.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to one domain, global history knowledge, and one question format built from the Seshat Databank.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4-turbo, GPT-4o, Llama-3-70B, Llama-3.1-70B (FP8), Llama-3.1-8B (FP8) and Gemini-1.5-flash.

quantitative_metrics.note: Balanced accuracy, adjusted balanced accuracy, and bootstrap 95% confidence intervals; exact match against the key.

published_after_march_2023.note: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks track; evaluations run in August 2024.

summary: The paper introduces HiST-LLM, a multiple-choice benchmark derived from the Seshat Global History Databank (36,000 data points, 600+ polities, 2,700+ references). Seven LLMs are evaluated with few-shot chain-of-thought prompts. The results are broken down by time period, world region and variable category.
key_findings: Four-choice balanced accuracy ranges from 33.6% (Llama-3.1-8B) to 46.0% (GPT-4-Turbo), against 25% for random guessing. Two-choice balanced accuracy ranges from 57.6% to 63.2% (GPT-4o best). Performance declines toward recent periods. Regional performance is more even, best for the Americas and lowest for Oceania and Sub-Saharan Africa.
evaluation_unit: Seshat data point converted into a multiple-choice question
gold_upstream: Seshat Global History Databank (Turchin et al. 2015 [10]); per this paper, research assistants supervised by established scholars coded values with justifications and citations, and 14,000 of the 36,000 data points underwent expert review.
facets_explanation: Reference answers are the coded Seshat values (present, absent, inferred present, inferred absent). They were produced by graduate-level research assistants under supervision of scholars, with expert review for 14,000 of 36,000 points. Questions give only the variable, polity and time frame, so the answer needs outside historical knowledge. Scoring is exact match against one key. The paper does not discuss annotator disagreement as a plurality issue.
results_explanation: Table 1 gives GPT-4-turbo 46.0 [45.5, 46.5] as the best 4-choice balanced accuracy, which is the headline figure and is reported as balanced accuracy (mapped to 'accuracy'). The same items scored on only Present/Absent give Llama-3.1-8B 57.6 versus 33.6 on 4 choices, a 24-point gap. That is the largest such difference, derived by subtraction. Table 3 shows lowest performance in Oceania and Sub-Saharan Africa. No human baseline is reported.
